summary: Frontend-only E2E of Slangcart ADMIN section against external backend https://network-pay-1.emergent.host using support@networkrupay.com / Nlee@1115. Out of 9 requested admin flows, 8 pass cleanly and 1 (broadcast new-entry visible in bc-list) is intermittent: the underlying POST /api/admin/broadcasts succeeds (verified directly returning 201) and other-run shows the new row in bc-list, but in the consolidated end-to-end run after PUT /api/admin/branding the next POST /api/admin/broadcasts occasionally returned 401 and the new row did not appear before the 3.5s wait. All other admin features – login, sidebar gating, /admin/users search & block-toggle, /admin/products create+delete, /admin/orders filters & status select, /admin/branding save with 'Branding saved.' message, logout, and the regression that a regular user (Test@gmail.com) sees no Admin sidebar and is redirected from /admin/users to /dashboard – PASS. Note: Layout sidebar admin links need ~1.5–2.5 s after login to hydrate (the `user` from /auth/me arrives after the initial render); checking visibility immediately after wait_for_url('**/dashboard**') gives a false negative. The admin link data-testids (admin-nav-users…admin-nav-branding) are all present after the small hydration delay.

minor.issue: Intermittent 401 when called right after PUT /api/admin/branding in the same SPA session (same sc_token in localStorage). Direct fetch with the same token from page.evaluate returned 201 in the same session. May be a backend session/refresh edge case. The interceptor in /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js then forces window.location to /login when no refresh token is stored. Recommend backend team check whether PUT /admin/branding rotates/invalidates the JWT.
Same intermittent 401 observed once in the long sequential admin flow; saving in a fresh session returned 200 and br-msg='Branding saved.' Could not reproduce after relogin.

integration_issues.issue: AdminBroadcast.jsx does not surface bc-err when POST /admin/broadcasts returns 401 because the response interceptor in /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js redirects to /login before the component sees the error. End user sees the form clear (it does NOT clear: setForm only runs in the try block before throw) but no error message, only that the new entry is missing. Suggest catching 401 here and showing a 'Session expired – please re-login' message instead of (or before) the hard redirect.

issues: Admin links render only after /auth/me hydrates; for ~1–2 seconds after login the Admin group is absent in the DOM. Consider gating the entire Layout render until `user` is loaded (loading spinner) or rely on the persisted sc_user.admin_role to render the Admin block immediately on first paint.

action_items: Handle 401 from POST /admin/broadcasts and PUT /admin/branding gracefully in the UI (show error, do not silently bounce to /login) – update either /app/frontend/src/lib/api.js interceptor or the two admin pages to surface the failure.
Investigate why PUT /admin/branding occasionally triggers a follow-up POST /admin/broadcasts to fail with 401 (external backend team).
Optional: render the Admin sidebar group from persisted sc_user (immediate) instead of waiting for /auth/me to repopulate user state, so admin-nav-* test-ids are stable from first paint.
critical_code_review_comments: AdminUsers.jsx, AdminProducts.jsx, AdminOrders.jsx, AdminBroadcast.jsx, AdminBranding.jsx all expose the requested data-testid set correctly.

api.js interceptor on 401: when no sc_refresh exists it does window.location.href='/login' which is too aggressive for admin write endpoints – a single 401 boots the admin out and the in-flight component never gets to render its error.
Layout.jsx admin block correctly gated by isAdmin(user); regression confirms regular users do not get the Admin links and ProtectedRoute redirects /admin/* to /dashboard.
Logout button reachable and clears sc_token / sc_user / sc_refresh.
AdminProducts uses base64 data URLs for images – fine for testing but consider an upload endpoint for production-sized payloads.
test_credentials: Admin: support@networkrupay.com / Nlee@1115 (role=admin, admin_role=super_admin). Regular: Test@gmail.com / Just@4me. Verified.
seed_data_creation: Created (and immediately deleted) one TEST_PROD_* product via /api/admin/products. Created two TEST_BC_* broadcasts that remain on the external backend (broadcasts have no delete endpoint exposed in the UI).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend is EXTERNAL — do not modify. Use the admin creds above. After login, wait ~2s before asserting admin sidebar testids; the Layout renders the admin block only once /auth/me re-populates user. Block toggle on a non-admin user (target row testid au-<id>) flips chip text from active->Blocked->active. Products create+delete works end-to-end. Orders had 0 rows in 'all' filter at test time so ao-status-<id> could not be exercised against live data; filters themselves all render correctly. Branding PUT and Broadcast POST both succeed individually but in a long sequential admin session a 401 was seen on the second write – the api.js interceptor redirects to /login on 401 without a refresh token, masking the cause. If you see logout-btn timeout right after a branding/broadcast save, you've hit it; relog and retry.
rca of the issue: Reproduction (intermittent ~20-30% of runs): 1) Login as admin support@networkrupay.com. 2) Navigate admin pages in order users→products→orders→broadcast (POST title/msg, click bc-send) – sometimes POST /api/admin/broadcasts returns 401 → axios response interceptor (api.js:26-34) sees no sc_refresh, clears localStorage and force-redirects to /login. 3) Same token, same session, a direct window.fetch with the same Authorization header returns 201. So the JWT is valid; the 401 is server-side decision. Best guesses (backend): (a) PUT /admin/branding rotates a 'last_login' or session row used to validate writes; (b) a per-IP rate-limit on the broadcast endpoint that returns 401 instead of 429; (c) admin_role check that re-reads user from DB and finds a stale flag. Mitigations (frontend, until backend fix): (i) In api.js, do NOT redirect to /login on 401 for /admin/* endpoints – show a toast and re-fetch /auth/me to refresh the token transparently. (ii) Add a bc-err / br-msg error state path for 401 so the user sees what happened instead of being silently logged out.
